purpose: Capture only implementation-discovered design gaps or semantic conflicts after product design scope closure.

items.current_design_semantics: 88 SS2 defines EXPLICIT_ID as 'FR-COM, FR-META, NFR-* 등 명시 ID'. Separately, the semantic-assurance companion set defines SA-01~14 (Semantic Assurance Capability) and XC-01~30 (Cross-Cutting Control) as its own explicit ID vocabulary, used pervasively (189 SA-* and 13+ XC-* subtype mentions across docs/master/semantic-assurance). 90 SS3's trace node list (REQUIREMENT, DESIGN, CONTRACT, OPERATION, API, EVENT, RECEIPT, TEST, FIXTURE, EVIDENCE_TYPE, POLICY, AUTHORITY_RULE, UI_CLAIM, FINDING) has no CAPABILITY or CONTROL node type.
items.implementation_conflict_or_new_semantics: generate-requirement-universe.py (RU-02) only extracts FR-COM-*, FR-META-*, FR-FRESH-*, NFR-* as EXPLICIT_ID requirements, per 88 SS2's literal examples. SA-*/XC-* IDs are excluded from the Requirement Universe entirely for Batch 0. It is undefined whether each SA-*/XC-* item IS a Requirement (and should get its own requirement_id, e.g. as CONTRACT_REQUIRED or a new source class), or whether it is a distinct artifact type that requirements merely reference (design_refs), or whether it should map 1:1 onto FR-META-*/FR-COM-* records that already exist. Guessing this would risk either silently inflating the denominator with a artifact class the design docs never authorized as EXPLICIT_ID, or silently omitting a real requirement source, either of which 137 SS5 prohibits ('구현 편의를 위해 requirement/design 의미를 축소 삭제 금지').
items.proposed_disposition: Recommend a human/design decision in a future companion doc (e.g. a 88-addendum or new SS in 92) explicitly stating whether SA-*/XC-* are (a) a 7th Requirement Source Class, (b) CONTRACT_REQUIRED-derived requirements owned by their parent FR-META entry, or (c) a separate CAPABILITY/CONTROL trace node type to be added to 90 SS3. Until resolved, RU-02 continues to exclude SA-*/XC-* from EXPLICIT_ID extraction; this does not block Batch 0 EVIDENCE_READY because 88 SS2's literal examples do not name SA-*/XC-* as requirement sources.

items.current_design_semantics: Four different, mutually inconsistent enumerations exist for what 88 and 11 both literally call 'Requirement source class' (or 92's 'taxonomy', same concept): (1) 88 SS2: EXPLICIT_ID|PROGRAM_FUNCTION|ACCEPTANCE_CRITERION|INVARIANT|POLICY_REQUIRED|CONTRACT_REQUIRED|REGULATORY_REQUIRED (an extraction-origin axis). (2) 92 SS2 'taxonomy': FUNCTIONAL|NON_FUNCTIONAL|ASSURANCE|SECURITY|PRIVACY|OPERATIONAL|DEPLOYMENT|AI_SPECIFIC|REGULATORY|COMMERCIAL_CONTRACTUAL (a subject-matter axis). (3) 11 SS6.2 'Source class' (RequirementUniverseV2): BUSINESS|CONTRACT|POLICY|CODE|CONFIG|ARCHITECTURE|DATA|API|SECURITY|PRIVACY|OPERATIONS|RIGHTS|FAILURE_RECOVERY|RUNTIME_BEHAVIOR|EXTERNAL_STANDARD (a third, larger vocabulary blending origin and subject axes). (4) The already-existing contracts/requirement-universe-snapshot.candidate.v2.schema.json's 'source_classes' field: BUSINESS|FUNCTIONAL|NON_FUNCTIONAL|SECURITY_PRIVACY_LEGAL|ARCHITECTURE_DATA|RUNTIME_DEPLOYMENT|AI_AGENT_MODEL|INFERRED|EXTERNAL_STANDARD|OPERATION_RECOVERY (a fourth, differently-blended vocabulary already shipped as a real machine contract). No document states a mapping or supersession relationship between any of these four.
items.implementation_conflict_or_new_semantics: Batch 0's requirement-record.v2.schema.json implemented (1) as source_class and (2) as taxonomy as two SEPARATE fields on the same record, treating them as orthogonal axes -- this was my own resolution choice, made before discovering (3) and (4) also claim the 'source class' name for yet other vocabularies. It is now unclear whether: (a) 88/92's two-axis split is the intended final design and 11/the existing candidate schema are stale/superseded drafts, (b) 11's Bundle D (TargetManifestV2/RequirementUniverseV2) is meant to fully replace 88/89/90/91/92's RU flow rather than coexist with it (in which case Batch 0's whole RU-01..RU-07 implementation may need to migrate to 11's vocabulary), or (c) the existing shipped requirement-universe-snapshot.candidate.v2.schema.json is a DIFFERENT contract for a DIFFERENT purpose (target-Program-scoped SA-02 requirement discovery, vs. Batch 0's ONSure-own-product requirement universe) that only coincidentally reuses the same field name. This is a DENOMINATOR_SEMANTIC-class conflict per 89 SS6 (P0 class) because it directly determines what counts in the Requirement Universe denominator.
items.proposed_disposition: Requires a human/design-authority decision: which document (88+92, or 11) is canonical for Requirement source classification, and whether contracts/requirement-universe-snapshot.candidate.v2.schema.json is the same concept as Batch 0's requirement-universe-snapshot.v2.schema.json (in which case one must supersede the other) or a genuinely distinct target-scoped contract (in which case both may coexist under different names, and 89's naming-canonicalization rule SS5 should be applied so the names stop colliding). Until resolved, no further contract in this lineage should invent a fifth vocabulary or silently pick one of the four.

resolution.disposition: DCQ-0002 was not one enum with four competing versions; it was two distinct Requirement Universe objects colliding under the same name. (A) Product Design Requirement Universe -- authority 88+92, purpose: ONSure's own product-design QA denominator, canonical names ProductDesignRequirementUniverse/ProductDesignRequirementUniverseSnapshot, fields source_class (88's 7 values) and taxonomy (92's 10 values) kept as two separate, non-merged axes. (B) Target Assurance Requirement Universe -- authority 11 Bundle D, purpose: the requirement denominator of the customer/target Program ONSure verifies, canonical names TargetAssuranceRequirementUniverse/TargetAssuranceRequirementUniverseSnapshot, using 11's 15-value source vocabulary. The pre-existing contracts/requirement-universe-snapshot.candidate.v2.schema.json (has target_id + target discovery fields) is classified as a Target Assurance candidate, not a Product Design contract, and remains non-authoritative pending an explicit mapping/migration to 11's vocabulary. Batch 0's source_class+taxonomy split is confirmed correct for (A) and unchanged. Batch 1's TargetManifest/RequirementUniverse work proceeds under identity (B) with distinct names -- it does not reuse Product Design schema names, and it does not invent a fifth vocabulary. Product Design exact population/applicability/trace/orphan/SHA-256 inventory/registry digest remain open under a separate Design QA gate, not blocked by this resolution.

gate: Any unresolved P0 blocks the affected batch from EVIDENCE_READY.
anti_recursion: Do not create new product-design axes unless an implementation-discovered gap cannot be owned by an existing design authority.
